subject: Money
title: Charm Pricing
description: A quick win: understand Charm Pricing.

hook.text: $9.99 instead of $10. One cent difference. But sales increase 8-20%. The brain reads left to right.

buildup.text: We process the first digit most. $9.99 registers as 'nine something.' $10.00 registers as 'ten.'

discovery.text: MIT tested identical products at $34, $39, and $44. The $39 item outsold the $34 one. Magic number.

twist.text: Luxury brands avoid .99 pricing. Round numbers feel premium. $1,000 says quality; $999 says discount.

climax.text: The penny trick is over 100 years old. It still works because the brain shortcut never updates.

punchline.text: One penny buys a whole digit of illusion.

quiz.question: Why does $9.99 feel cheaper than $10.00?
options: The brain processes the first digit most
